scope.domain: QASkills CLI, SDK, agent detection, framework detection, command behavior, filesystem delivery, and npm release
scope.selectionRule: Each survivor has a distinct searcher need, direct implementation evidence, enough test and workflow depth for a 3000-word article, and no slug, title, primary-keyword, or intent collision.

survivors.answerFirstQuestion: How do you install a local SKILL.md package with QASkills and verify the copied files without contacting the registry?
survivors.intentBoundary: User workflow for local filesystem input only, not registry fallback, GitHub extraction, or custom destination setup.

survivors.answerFirstQuestion: How should QASkills installation tests prove that an untrusted skill name cannot escape the intended agent skills directory?
survivors.intentBoundary: Security containment of the final destination path, not temporary-name cleanup or ordinary --dir behavior.

survivors.answerFirstQuestion: What happens when QASkills installs to several agents and one filesystem copy fails partway through the loop?
survivors.intentBoundary: Failure consistency across several destinations, not source download fallback or one custom directory.

survivors.answerFirstQuestion: How does QASkills distinguish home-directory agents from project-directory agents when resolving configuration and skill paths?
survivors.intentBoundary: Scope classification and path resolution, not the separate config-file fallback or universal target.

survivors.answerFirstQuestion: How can you test that QASkills detects a project agent from its config file when its config directory does not exist?
survivors.intentBoundary: The configFile fallback branch for project agents only, not scope classification or skills-directory status.

survivors.titleTag: Use the Universal Agent Skills Directory
survivors.answerFirstQuestion: Why does QASkills always expose the universal ~/.agents/skills destination even when no vendor-specific agent configuration is detected?
survivors.intentBoundary: Cross-vendor destination behavior, not vendor-specific install guides or generic agent scope detection.

survivors.answerFirstQuestion: How does QASkills report an agent whose configuration exists but whose skills directory has not been created yet?
survivors.intentBoundary: The DetectedAgent.exists signal after successful agent detection, not a missing agent config or list-command read failure.

survivors.answerFirstQuestion: How can qaskills add target a supported agent by ID even when that agent was not discovered on the current filesystem?
survivors.intentBoundary: Explicit installation to one known but absent agent, not automatic detection or unknown-agent rejection.
